candidates.summary: Jepsen (Kyle Kingsbury) published its analysis of ParticleDB, a multi-model database for AI workloads built by a small Orkes team with heavy LLM assistance, reporting 96 issues and a dedicated section on the tradeoffs of LLM-built software.
facts: Jepsen tested ParticleDB 1.1.4 through 1.1.18.11.rc-22 and found its 'Full ACID' claims 'somewhat premature', presenting 96 issues from crashes, deadlocks and data loss to dropped tables re-emerging and strings turning into integers.
Report: 'LLM tooling repeatedly claimed that bugs had been fixed when, in fact, they had not.'
Report: Orkes 'seemed unable to explain the causes or resolutions of nearly every issue we found in ParticleDB'; new builds arrived without changelogs.
Report: 'the use of LLMs erodes trust in documentation, in software, and in the organizations which produce them.'

As of 1.1.18.11.rc-22, append and rw workloads still found anomalies in every transaction mode; ParticleDB claimed to be '1087x faster than PostgreSQL', but Jepsen saw throughput decline linearly over an hour.
Simon Willison quoted the LLM passage on Nov 1; Hacker News thread at 310 points.

candidates.summary: Armin Ronacher (@mitsuhiko, creator of Flask) posted that he believes an Opus 5.5 agent could re-implement all of CPython in about two weeks without human input, working only against the tests, and in a follow-up argued agents do better building their own test suite for porting than relying on an existing one.
facts: Post: 'you could have an Opus 5.5 agent re-implement all of CPython probably within two weeks without any human input, against just the tests, and probably with full compatibility with including ABI, no GIL, a jit'.

Follow-up: 'you don't actually need a test suite to rebuild something. In fact, you're probably better off having the agent builds its own test suite specifically for porting'; he says pre-existing tests are often bad for hill climbing.
He cites a recent case where an agent re-implemented Excel's formula engine and built its own test suite from scratch.
This is an opinion and prediction, not a completed project.

candidates.summary: An HKUST PhD student, Jiahao Shao, posted that Anthropic flagged his account for 'training a competitor' and now blocks anything touching RFT, SFT or training larger models, although he says Claude only helped submit jobs and run analysis and he never distilled Claude.
facts: Post text: 'I never distilled Claude—rollouts came from a strong open-source model; Claude just helped submit jobs and run analysis. Still got tagged for "training a competitor," and now anything touching RFT, SFT, or training larger models gets me blocked'.
The post reached 3,467 likes and about 255K views; the Hacker News thread 'Anthropic blocks users for anything touching training larger models' reached 429 points.
Single first-hand account; no public Anthropic response found on X at capture time.

candidates.summary: Designer Benji Taylor released Stageshow, an open agent skill that helps coding agents make better faux UI stills, animations and bento grids; Meng To shared it on Nov 1 saying it will help avoid AI slop.
facts: Install: 'npx skills add benjitaylor/skills --skill stageshow'; the page says it works with Grok Build, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other agents.

The skill contains SKILL.md (five ways faux UI fails, a seven-step workflow), reference docs on craft, motion and framing, dozens of gold examples, a small React kit, and scripts that film a demo and check frames and layout.
Output is an ordinary React component; the author says most demos still take a few rounds of feedback.
Launch post: 9,997 likes and 17,093 bookmarks; Meng To's share: 416 likes and 616 bookmarks.
